The wave redirecting system includes a lower frame body having first and second upper surfaces. An upper frame body, which also has first and second upper surfaces, is connected to or formed integrally with the lower frame body. The upper frame body is oriented relative to the lower frame body so as to define first and second angles between the respective frame bodies.

A plurality of anchor feet is connected to, or formed integrally with, a bottom surface of the lower frame body. The anchor feet are configured to secure and stabilize the wave redirecting system on a supporting surface. In addition, at least one redirecting blade is attached to one or both of the first and second upper surfaces of the upper frame body. The redirecting blade is positioned relative to the upper frame body so as to define a third angle, thereby facilitating the redirection of waves incident on the system.
outputs.L4:
The wave-redirecting system is designed to reduce the impact of incoming waves on shorelines, coastal structures, and other marine installations. The system includes a lower frame body connected to an angled upper frame body, forming a rigid support assembly capable of withstanding repeated hydrodynamic loading. The lower frame body provides a stable base, while the upper frame body extends upward at a selected inclination corresponding to the desired wave-redirection characteristics.

One or more anchor feet are attached to the lower frame body. These feet engage the seabed, shoreline, or another supporting surface to resist sliding, lifting, and overturning forces generated by waves and currents. Depending on site conditions, the anchor feet may be embedded, weighted, fastened to a foundation, or used with supplemental anchoring components. The frame bodies and anchor feet may be formed from corrosion-resistant metal, reinforced concrete, composite material, or another material suitable for prolonged exposure to a marine environment.

A redirecting blade is mounted on the angled upper frame body at a defined angle. When an incoming wave encounters the blade, the blade changes the direction of at least a portion of the wave flow, directing water and associated energy upward, seaward, laterally, or along another predetermined path. The blade angle may be fixed or adjustable to accommodate different wave climates, water depths, installation locations, and protection objectives. Its shape, width, curvature, and orientation may also be selected to control the manner in which wave energy is redirected.

By combining a securely anchored lower structure with an inclined upper support and a properly oriented redirecting blade, the system manages wave forces without relying solely on the absorption or dissipation of wave energy. Multiple systems may be installed individually or arranged in rows or arrays to protect a larger area. The resulting configuration provides a stable and durable solution for shoreline stabilization, erosion reduction, harbor protection, marine infrastructure protection, and related coastal applications.
outputs.L5:
### A Wave Redirecting

A wave moves toward the shore with quiet certainty, carrying the force of distant winds. Then it meets a wall of stone. For a moment, its journey seems finished—but the water turns, divides, and finds another direction. Part of it rises into spray, part flows along the rocks, and part returns to the sea.

Redirecting is not the same as surrendering. Like the wave, we sometimes encounter obstacles that make our original path impossible. Yet movement can continue in a new form. A changed direction may reveal unexpected shores, fresh possibilities, and a strength we did not know we possessed.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a wave redirecting system with lower and upper frame bodies, anchor feet, and an angled redirecting blade.
counterfactuals.output: A wave redirecting system includes a lower frame body, an upper frame body coupled to and supported above the lower frame body, and a plurality of anchor feet configured to secure the system relative to a supporting surface. An angled redirecting blade is mounted between the lower and upper frame bodies and presents an inclined wave-engaging surface. The redirecting blade is oriented to receive incident wave energy and direct at least a portion of the wave flow along a predetermined path, thereby reducing, dispersing, or changing the direction of wave forces acting downstream of the system. The frame bodies maintain the position and angular orientation of the redirecting blade, while the anchor feet resist displacement caused by hydrodynamic loading. The system may be installed individually or in an array and may include adjustable or modular components for varying blade angle, spacing, and wave-redirection characteristics.

counterfactuals.output:
### Wave-Deflecting Structure

A wave-deflecting structure comprising: a lower frame; an upper frame coupled to the lower frame and extending at an oblique angle relative thereto; a plurality of anchoring feet coupled to the lower frame and configured to secure the wave-deflecting structure to a supporting surface; and at least one blade mounted on at least one of a first upper surface and a second upper surface of the upper frame, the at least one blade being configured to intercept and redirect incident wave energy.

### Exemplary Claims

1. **A wave-deflecting structure, comprising:**  
   a lower frame;  
   an upper frame coupled to the lower frame and oriented at an oblique angle relative to the lower frame, the upper frame having a first upper surface and a second upper surface;  
   a plurality of anchoring feet coupled to the lower frame and configured to anchor the wave-deflecting structure to a support substrate; and  
   at least one blade mounted on at least one of the first upper surface or the second upper surface and configured to deflect waves incident upon the wave-deflecting structure.

2. The wave-deflecting structure of claim 1, wherein the at least one blade comprises a plurality of blades.

3. The wave-deflecting structure of claim 1, wherein at least one blade is mounted on each of the first upper surface and the second upper surface.

4. The wave-deflecting structure of claim 1, wherein the anchoring feet extend outwardly from the lower frame.

5. The wave-deflecting structure of claim 1, wherein the upper frame is fixedly coupled to the lower frame.

6. The wave-deflecting structure of claim 1, wherein the upper frame is adjustably coupled to the lower frame such that the oblique angle is selectively variable.

7. The wave-deflecting structure of claim 1, wherein the blade projects outwardly from the corresponding upper surface and is oriented to redirect incident waves away from an area protected by the wave-deflecting structure.
